items.text: It is known that taking a photo of wildlife requires a great deal of patience, confidence, and precision. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet the factor that many do not consider is preparedness. <break time="0.8s" /> Before you face your animal subject, you should study and learn about it so that you can anticipate its behavior. <break time="0.8s" /> For example, photographing the incredible migration of baby turtles from their nest to their new home in the sea may depend on luck. <break time="0.8s" /> If you want to get a shot of their momentous journey, you ought to learn about them as much as possible, including the fact that they usually travel during the cool, dark nights of July. <break time="0.8s" /> Genuine knowledge about the animal you wish to capture through your lens not only increases the likelihood of success but makes the slow time in the field much more enjoyable.
